The board has \(5\times 4=20\) unit squares, and each tile covers \(4\) squares, so at most \(20/4=5\) tiles could fit.

Suppose \(5\) tiles fit. Color the \(5\times4\) board like a chessboard. It has \(10\) black and \(10\) white squares. Each T-shaped tile covers either \(3\) black \(+1\) white or \(1\) black \(+3\) white, giving a black–white imbalance of \(\pm2\). With \(5\) tiles, the total imbalance would be a sum of five numbers each equal to \(\pm2\). To match the board’s equal black and white counts, we would need equally many tiles of each type, impossible with an odd number \(5\). Hence \(5\) tiles cannot fit.

Four tiles can fit: place them in a \(4\times4\) pinwheel pattern inside the \(5\times4\) rectangle, leaving one entire column empty. For example,
\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
A&A&A&B&.\\
D&A&B&B&.\\
D&D&C&B&.\\
D&C&C&C&.
\end{array}
\]
Each letter forms one rotated T-tile, with no overlaps.

Therefore, the maximum number is
\[
\boxed{4}
\]
